Textiles as a design medium
YEAR 9 TEXTILES · MODULE 2
UNDERSTAND THE IDEA

The five focus areas are apparel, furnishings, costume, textile art and non-apparel. They organise the different end uses of textile design.
Textile fibres, yarns and fabrics can be used as a design medium. Their flexible structures can be selected and manipulated for many products.
Purpose and user needs guide material and process choices. A successful item must perform for its intended end use.

THEORY 2 OF 3
Elements of design
YEAR 9 TEXTILES · MODULE 2
UNDERSTAND THE IDEA

Line, direction, shape, size, colour, value and texture are design elements. They are visual tools used to communicate and develop ideas.
Elements can be isolated or combined. Designers control emphasis and visual effect through their relationships.
Texture describes a surface's visual or tactile quality. It affects how an item looks and can affect how it feels.

Sources of inspiration and mood boards
textPreview: Sources of inspiration and mood boards

text: YEAR 9 TEXTILES · MODULE 2
UNDERSTAND THE IDEA

History, culture, nature, manufactured items, events and emotions can inspire design. A broad source range helps designers generate varied directions.
Inspiration is transformed rather than copied. Original design develops selected features for a new purpose.
A mood board communicates a coherent direction. Related images, colours and textures make the intended mood visible.
